original_question: For the flat hierarchy in which flat crossings are labeled by elements of an ordinal alpha and a flat third Reidemeister move allows a strand with two labels a to slide across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b, classify the resulting diagrams and determine how this hierarchy generalizes ordinary flat virtual-knot theory.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core content of the paper’s actual open problem almost verbatim: the hierarchy is defined for an ordinal α, flat crossings are labeled by elements of α, the flat third Reidemeister move is restricted so that a strand carrying two equal labels a may pass a crossing labeled b only when a > b, and the research task is to classify the resulting hierarchy.
missing_details: The paper’s actual task is to classify equivalence classes of diagrams in the hierarchy; the phrase about 'determining how this hierarchy generalizes ordinary flat virtual-knot theory' is explanatory background in the paper, not a separate open problem.
The ambient objects are flat virtual diagrams in the sense of Section 2.2, so virtual crossings remain part of the theory and retain the usual detour move.
The relevant equivalence relation is the generalized flat Reidemeister equivalence from Section 2.2, with the third move modified by the label-order restriction stated in Problem 3.
The quantifier is 'for any ordinal α' (equivalently, for each fixed ordinal α one obtains such a hierarchy).
The paper speaks of classifying 'diagrams' in this hierarchy, not only knots; links and more general flat virtual diagrams are included in the scope.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions occur here; this is a purely diagrammatic/combinatorial classification problem.
refined_question: For each ordinal α, consider flat virtual diagrams in the sense of Section 2.2—i.e. diagrams with virtual crossings and flat crossings, taken up to the generalized flat Reidemeister I and II moves together with the usual virtual detour moves—but now with every flat crossing labeled by an element of α and with the flat Reidemeister III move allowed only when the sliding strand carries two equal labels a and the crossed flat crossing has label b with a > b. Classify the equivalence classes of diagrams in this α-indexed flat hierarchy.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 8.1, Problem 3, since it reproduces the problem’s defining data almost word for word: labels from an ordinal α and the restricted flat Reidemeister III move. To make the question stand-alone without broadening it, one must import the local setup from Section 2.2, where the paper defines flat virtual diagrams and their generalized flat Reidemeister equivalence, including the role of virtual crossings and detour moves. The phrase about generalizing ordinary flat virtual-knot theory should remain descriptive rather than become a second research objective, because the paper already states that this hierarchy is such a generalization; the actual open problem is classification. The paper presents this as a listed research problem, not as a theorem or conjecture, and it notes Manturov’s 'Flat hierarchy' as an initial step.
